docs.title: CRISPREvo user guide
docs.text: CRISPREvo helps you prepare CRISPR data, compare spacer arrays, infer strain relationships, search candidate spacer targets and make integrated tree–array figures. Start from the material you already have; you do not need to run every tool.

docs.title: Workflow overview
docs.text: View the workflow at full size.

docs.title: Choose a tool
docs.text:
What you want to do Tool guide What to provide What you get Retrieve sequence records SeqFetcher NCBI sequence/assembly accessions or sequence UIDs FASTA and source metadata Detect arrays or filter detector results CRISPRPrep Genome FASTA, NCBI nucleotide/assembly IDs or CRISPRCasFinder JSON Processed spacer CSV and filtering report Infer relationships among strains CRISPRPhylo Processed spacer CSV for multiple strains Strain tree, optional array-tree ZIP and images Compare spacer order and sharing SpacerMap Numbered arrays or spacer sequence data Array figure, ID–sequence lookup, occurrence statistics and cluster network Display arrays beside a tree ArrayPhyloViz Newick plus numbered arrays or SpacerMap SVG Annotated figure and editable project Find candidate sequence targets SpacerTarget Original spacer sequences with sample identities Match table, strain–target network and search report

Each guide explains input preparation, exact page controls, parameter choices, result interpretation, downloads and common problems. Button names follow the current interface: CRISPRPrep uses Run, SpacerTarget uses Search, and the other tools use Commit (the CRISPRPhylo control may read Build tree after a run).

docs.title: First visit
docs.text: Follow the quick start for a small, reproducible plotting example, then the end-to-end workflow for real multi-strain data. The input reference explains which file belongs in which tool; downloads explains what to keep.

docs.title: Before interpreting an analysis
docs.text:
Check sample identities, retained data and the settings applied to the result. Shared spacer IDs describe the chosen numbering scheme; a tree describes the selected inference; a target match describes sequence similarity under the selected search and filters. The tool guides explain these distinctions with examples.

Save Copy results link once a Job ID appears. Accepted analyses continue on the server after closing the tab, and My Jobs restores results from all six tools. Results expire seven days after the task ends; download important outputs and retain original inputs/settings. In ArrayPhyloViz, save a new private snapshot or project JSON after further edits. See troubleshooting for recovery help.

docs.title: Citing CRISPREvo
docs.text:
A formal CRISPREvo manuscript citation is not yet provided here. Use the source repository and the exact software version for attribution until a preferred citation becomes available.

Until then, cite the CRISPREvo source repository and record the exact release tag or Git commit used:

CRISPREvo: CRISPR evolutionary analysis web platform. Source code: https://github.com/zwxyo/crisprevo

docs.title: Underlying tools and services
docs.text:
Cite the methods used in your run as appropriate:

  • CRISPRCasFinder for CRISPR detection.
  • NCBI records, E-utilities and NCBI Datasets for retrieved sequences and assemblies.
  • NCBI BLAST and target accessions for SpacerTarget searches; retain search date, database, hit limit, filters and the report.
  • The GraphMSA or CRISPRFormer method used for tree inference, once the project-specific preferred citations are supplied.

The documentation structure and task-oriented style were informed by the CRISPR Comparison Toolkit documentation, particularly its separation of quick usage, tutorials, input contracts, and tool-specific pages. CRISPREvo behavior described here is based on the current CRISPREvo web implementation.

docs.title: Information to record
docs.text: For reproducibility, report the CRISPREvo release/commit, access date, input source, processing settings, SpacerMap alignment and clustering, color seed, tree method, repeat-distance setting, CRISPRFormer profile where applicable, any chosen root, and manual edits made in ArrayPhyloViz. Keep original inputs, settings and downloaded outputs separately: private results links expire after seven days, and saved reports do not retain every submitted parameter.

docs.title: My Jobs: save, retrieve and download results
docs.text: Use My Jobs (/my-jobs) to return to work from all six tools without an account. Each submitted analysis receives a full Job ID and private results link. Keep that link: the browser history is a convenience, not the result archive.

docs.title: Save access when submitting
docs.text:
1. Submit the input in the tool and wait until a Job ID and private link appear. Do not close the page while it is still uploading or submitting.
  2. Select Copy results link and save it with your sample notes.
  3. Once the job is accepted, you can close the page. Server processing continues.
  4. Open the saved link later, or use My Jobs → Retrieve a job to paste the full ID or link and select Retrieve.

Individual tool pages also offer Retrieve previous results. If an ID belongs to another tool, the shared retrieval control directs you to that job's results page. Use the full 32-character ID, not a shortened display fragment.

In ArrayPhyloViz, Commit composes the figure and attempts to save an initial project snapshot. After further edits, select Save changes again to create a new snapshot with a new ID. An older link does not automatically acquire later edits. Save project downloads JSON for local reopening and long-term storage.

docs.title: Understand status before interpreting a result
docs.text:
Status Meaning and action Queued Accepted and waiting to start. Keep the link; do not repeatedly submit the same input. Waiting for resources Accepted, but server capacity is temporarily insufficient. Input is retained while waiting, with no result-expiry timestamp yet. Wait for the existing job; queue position may be shown. Running Processing is in progress. Read the current phase; an activity bar is not a reliable completion-time estimate. Finished Processing ended successfully. Open the results and check their actual content; an empty biological result can still be a successful run. Partially finished Some inputs or steps failed while others produced output. Review the failed IDs/batches before interpreting coverage of the dataset. Failed / Cancelled Processing stopped. Available partial output can still be downloaded; a new analysis requires resubmitting input. Unavailable The job could not be retrieved. Check the full link, service availability and expiry.

A busy-service error before a Job ID appears means the submission was not accepted. Wait for the displayed retry interval, then submit again. This differs from an accepted job waiting in the queue.

docs.title: Browse the history
docs.text:
Filter by Tool, Status or job name/ID. Select the Submitted heading to switch newest/oldest first, and use Previous / Next for the six-row pages. Times are shown in your local time zone. Refresh checks current status.

Action What it does View Opens the job's results page. Copy link Copies the private results link. Download Downloads the saved result report when available; this is not every tool-specific export. Review results Opens a failed, partial or cancelled job to inspect available evidence. Remove Removes the reference from browser history only. It neither cancels nor deletes the server job. Export job links Downloads all links in this browser history, including entries hidden by filters. It does not download result data.

SpacerMap alignment/clustering changes update the preview without replacing the saved job; download the current SVG or commit a new job to retain them.

On the results page, use Open results to restore the interactive tool and access its exports. The page also offers Download result report and a primary output where supported: processed CSV, FASTA, Newick, SpacerMap SVG or project JSON. For CRISPRPhylo array-tree ZIP, reopen the interactive tool. For SpacerMap occurrence charts and statistics CSV, reopen SpacerMap and use the Spacer occurrence panel; the primary SVG download is the array map.

docs.title: Use another device
docs.text:
History is kept for the current browser tab by default. Enable Remember job history on this device to keep references across visits on that device. Turning it off removes the persistent history copy, not the server results.

History does not synchronize automatically. Open a saved link on the other device, or copy lines from Export job links into Retrieve a job. Up to 100 links/IDs can be imported at once. Anyone with a private link can access the job, so share links only with intended collaborators.

docs.title: Retention and reproducibility
docs.text:
Results and job records expire seven days after the task ends, including partial, failed and cancelled tasks. The results page displays an expiry time when available. Input workspaces are deleted at task completion; retrieving a result does not restore every original upload, parameter or run log.

Keep original inputs and a separate record of settings. CRISPRPrep results retain CSVs, counts, warnings and generated detection JSON when applicable, but uploaded JSON and processing options are not part of its saved result. For multi-sample detection, the processed CSV preserves sample grouping that is not embedded in the downloadable combined detector JSON; re-importing that JSON treats it as one sample. CRISPRPhylo retains the original inferred tree and method fields, but not the input CSV or run log. SpacerTarget retains match evidence and query IDs; original full query sequences and search parameters are removed from terminal job reports. Other outputs, such as fetched FASTA and saved figure projects, remain downloadable until expiry.

Download important files before expiry. Neither Remember job history, Export job links, nor opening a link extends retention. For a failed or cancelled analysis, submit your input again. SeqFetcher's Retry failed and Resume pending submit selected sets of IDs as new jobs; they do not modify the previous job. SpacerTarget has no in-place retry after completion.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This walkthrough uses small illustrative data so you can learn what the plots mean before processing a real dataset. The example Newick is supplied for practice; it is not a tree inferred from the numbered arrays.

docs.title: 1. Plot three arrays
docs.text:
Download example-arrays.txt, or paste:

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8
  1. Open SpacerMap from Analysis.
  2. Paste the text or upload the file, using only one input method.
  3. Keep Right alignment and explicitly select No clustering (the page initially selects Shared spacer).
  4. Select Commit.

You should see three rows, 9 distinct spacer labels and 6 shared labels. There are 17 spacer occurrences in total. IDs 3 and 7 occur only in strain A; ID 10 occurs only in strain C. Those array-specific types are triangles. Shared types connect across neighboring rows where applicable.

Try Ancestral spacer and wait for the automatic preview update: A and B share the rightmost ID 9, while C ends in 8 and forms its own group. Then try Shared spacer: all three arrays connect because every pair shares at least two distinct IDs. Show cluster network displays those links. This illustrates that different grouping rules answer different questions. Preview-only layout changes do not overwrite the saved job; download the current SVG or commit again to save a new result.

Choose SVG and Download SVG in the array-map export controls. Download numbered file is unnecessary for already numbered input; retain the example TXT.

Next, open Spacer occurrence → Show occurrence chart. IDs 2 and 6 should each have a bar height of 3; IDs 1, 9, 4 and 8 should each have height 2; IDs 3, 7 and 10 should each have height 1. In the matrix below the bars, filled circles mean present and hollow circles mean absent. Each array counts once per ID, even if that ID is repeated within it.

Select Download statistics CSV and compare it with the expected counts. Use this panel's own Format control to export the combined bar chart/matrix as SVG, PDF or another supported format. These statistics count arrays, not strains or total spacer copies. See the SpacerMap guide for the 50-ID chart limit and full interpretation.

docs.title: 2. Combine the arrays with a tree
docs.text:
Download example-tree.nwk, or copy:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);
  1. Open ArrayPhyloViz.
  2. Add the tree under Phylogenetic tree.
  3. Add the same arrays under CRISPR arrays, using the TXT or your exported SpacerMap SVG.
  4. Select Exact names, then Commit.
  5. Open Review and edit mapping: all three arrays should map to three leaves, with none unassigned.
  6. Adjust row spacing and label space. Turn on Use branch lengths to compare proportional lengths with the default topology layout.
  7. Keep the private link created by Commit. After edits, use Save changes again or Save project for a local JSON, then export SVG, PNG or PDF.

The tree groups A and B together. The array track helps inspect which types they share with each other and C. The internal label 95 came from the example tree; the editor did not calculate support. Reopen the saved JSON with Open saved project to continue editing.

docs.title: 3. Try data preparation and inference
docs.text:
For a detector-free trial, open CRISPRPrep → Load example → Import JSON results, keep the defaults and select Run. Examine retained/filtered arrays and the processed-row preview, then download Processed CSV and the report. To compare a different filter, load Import JSON results from Load example again (this resets options), change that filter and select Run for a new job. Keep a record of the settings for each result.

To try tree inference, open CRISPRPhylo → Load example, keep GraphMSA, then select Commit. This requires the site's inference service and can take time. Inspect the Newick source and download .nwk. Leave Repeat grouping distance at 0 for this first trial. Enable Also build array trees before submission if you also want the group-level ZIP. Do not substitute the other tools' built-in example buttons for this page's pasted three-array/Newick walkthrough: SpacerMap and ArrayPhyloViz load different examples. For your own cross-tool run, transfer or upload the same processed CSV and verify sample names.

docs.title: 4. Try sequence retrieval or target searching
docs.text:
SeqFetcher → Load example → Commit retrieves example nucleotide records from NCBI. Check metadata, keep the private results link, and download FASTA/ZIP for your records. For a whole-genome assembly, enter its GCA_/GCF_ accession with Nucleotide selected; one retrieved row may contain multiple FASTA contigs. These examples demonstrate retrieval, not bacterial CRISPR detection.

For SpacerTarget, use Load example or example-spacers.fasta, review the settings, then select Search. This submits a real NCBI search. Save Copy results link. Results depend on the database and search time, so no fixed hit count is expected. Follow the SpacerTarget guide to interpret Strict/Exact filters and network edges.

After a job is accepted, test recovery by copying its link into My Jobs → Retrieve a job. Open the result and confirm it is the expected dataset. Downloads and original inputs are still needed for long-term storage because server results expire after seven days.

Continue with the real-data workflow once input names and result types are familiar.

docs.title: The detector is unavailable
docs.text: Sequence detection requires the configured CRISPRCasFinder service to be available. Select Refresh status. If it remains unavailable, import a result.json generated elsewhere or ask the administrator to configure the detector command and working directory.

docs.title: A detection job disappeared
docs.text: Use My Jobs → Retrieve a job or Retrieve previous results and paste the full ID/private link. Default browser history is tab-local, but the accepted job remains on the server. Results expire seven days after the task ends; after expiry, submit your saved input again. See My Jobs for recovery and retention.

docs.title: JSON produced no spacer rows
docs.text: Check the evidence threshold, minimum spacer count, orientation fields, and N filter. Direct JSON import in SpacerMap applies fixed evidence 3/4 and ND/N rules; use CRISPRPrep for adjustable filtering and a detailed report.

docs.title: SpacerMap rejected the input
docs.text: Use one input method at a time. Numbered text must follow array_name<TAB>spacer1,spacer2,…. A direction-folder upload must contain FASTA files beneath a folder whose name includes pos/forward or neg/reverse.

docs.title: SpacerMap colors changed
docs.text: Keep the color seed unchanged and rerender. Archive the ID–sequence lookup to record the sequence-to-ID assignment, and the array-map SVG or normalized array text to retain array membership/order. Reuse the latter for plotting; the lookup alone is not array input.

docs.title: SpacerMap occurrence chart is disabled or statistics seem incomplete
docs.text:
Charts require 1–50 distinct spacer IDs. Above 50, preview and image export are unavailable; this is not a failed array-map run. Download statistics CSV still includes every ID, while View spacer counts displays the first 100. To chart a smaller dataset, submit a meaningful subset and identify it explicitly in your analysis.

Number of arrays counts each array once per ID. Repeated copies in one array do not add counts, and multiple arrays from one strain are counted separately. Counts use the last completed run; select Commit after editing input. If an older saved result lacks statistics, rerun the original or saved numbered input. If the statistics panel could not load, reload the page and retrieve the job; the main array-map workflow can still function.

docs.title: Scrolling no longer zooms the array or tree preview
docs.text: In SpacerMap's array/cluster previews and CRISPRPhylo, hold Ctrl while scrolling (Command on Mac). Ordinary scrolling moves the page. The occurrence chart has a scrollable preview instead of the array map's zoom/pan controls.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo rejected the CSV
docs.text: Confirm that the CSV contains the complete required header, at least two distinct nonempty Folder values, and at least two usable spacer rows. Negative arrays need a value in Reverse_Complement_Sequence.

docs.title: The tree pipeline timed out or is missing
docs.text: The web adapter stops a CRISPRPhylo run after 15 minutes. Reduce the dataset or run the underlying research pipeline outside the website. A missing script, model, or output-tree error requires administrator action on the server.

docs.title: Arrays did not match tree leaves
docs.text: ArrayPhyloViz matches original Newick leaf IDs rather than display labels or row order. Review exact spelling first, then try suffix removal or case/outer-space normalization. Ambiguous normalized names are deliberately left unmatched.

docs.title: SpacerMap's numbered download cannot reconstruct arrays
docs.text: Download numbered file contains Spacer_ID and Spacer_Sequence pairs, not array-per-line data. Use the array-map SVG for ArrayPhyloViz. For reusable array TXT, retrieve the SpacerMap job and copy its restored input text, or use the saved report's export_text. A number-only input cannot produce a sequence mapping; keep the original sequence data.

docs.title: Pasted genome FASTA is rejected
docs.text: CRISPRPrep paste mode requires >Sample Seq_Name Organism_Name for every record. A normal >contig_1 description file should be uploaded as a FASTA file or given an explicit sample field before pasting. Keep each sample/sequence pair unique and supply all three fields.

docs.title: An exported SVG cannot be reopened
docs.text: Use the array-map SVG from SpacerMap or the integrated figure SVG from ArrayPhyloViz, which carry supported editable metadata. Spacer occurrence charts and cluster-network SVGs do not contain editable array-map data. For older images, reopen the numbered array text and Newick source, or use a saved ArrayPhyloViz project JSON.

docs.title: A PNG export failed
docs.text: ArrayPhyloViz and CRISPRPhylo PNGs are limited to 32 million pixels and 16,000 pixels per side. Reduce PNG scale where available or export SVG. SpacerMap occurrence raster exports have a separate 40-million-pixel limit: reduce the statistics panel's DPI or use SVG/PDF. This does not bypass its 50-ID chart limit.

docs.title: Browser results disappeared after refresh
docs.text: Retrieve the saved private link to reopen server results. Unsaved ArrayPhyloViz edits and CRISPRPhylo root changes are local: save a project/snapshot or rerooted Newick before leaving. A result link restores the saved version only. Keeping browser history does not extend the seven-day server retention.

docs.title: SpacerTarget shows no matches
docs.text: Check whether all query batches completed. A partial/failed job is not evidence of no targets. Clear table filters, inspect All candidates TSV, and use Explore to inspect lower-coverage or lower-identity alignments. No returned matches refers only to the selected database, hit limit and search configuration.

docs.title: SpacerTarget table and network counts differ
docs.text: Rows are occurrence–site matches; edge weight counts different supporting sequences. Unassigned strains are omitted from the graph and only 200 nodes are displayed. Network type checkboxes can hide nodes without changing table/export filters. Use the filtered TSV to inspect all rows.

docs.title: A SpacerTarget task was interrupted
docs.text: Retrieve the full ID/link and review Details and any successful batches. Inputs are deleted at task end, so the current workflow requires resubmission of original spacers for a new search; there is no in-place Retry failed operation. Local waiting for resources and remote NCBI searching are separate stages. Use the displayed NCBI request link to inspect a submitted remote request, rather than repeatedly creating duplicate jobs.

docs.title: Fewer strains or arrays appear than expected
docs.text: In CRISPRPrep, uploaded FASTA files define samples by basename without extension, pasted headers define explicit Samples, and NCBI input uses requested accession IDs. Imported JSON uses its basename without .json, not its parent folder. Re-importing one combined detector JSON treats it as one sample; rerun the original input to preserve multi-sample grouping. Inspect Folder in the original processed CSV. SpacerMap CSV labels combine Folder_Seq_Name; check the resulting labels for collisions.

docs.title: SeqFetcher exported records hidden by search
docs.text: Search filters the table, not the selection. The header checkbox affects visible retrieved records; hidden selected rows remain selected. Check the selection count before export. Retry failed submits all failed IDs as a new job independently of row selection; save the earlier private link to retain access to successes.

docs.title: A job is waiting for resources
docs.text: If a Job ID is present, keep the link and wait for the accepted task. Inputs remain available while queued and the seven-day result-retention clock starts only when the task ends. If submission returned a busy response without an ID, wait for its retry interval and resubmit. If a job keeps waiting because its estimated resource requirement exceeds available capacity, ask the administrator to check capacity or cancel and submit a smaller dataset. The progress indicator shows activity and phases, not a guaranteed finish time.

docs.title: Assembly retrieval failed or returned several FASTA records
docs.text: Use Nucleotide for GCA_/GCF_ IDs. Several contigs under one assembly are expected; the length is their total. Check the failed-ID message for package/version/length validation and size limits. SeqFetcher uses one ID per request when assemblies are present; a single assembly exceeding the response limit still needs another workflow.

docs.title: CRISPRPrep cannot rerun with new settings after recovery
docs.text: Saved results retain outputs, not uploaded source JSON or processing options. Upload your original per-sample JSON again or rerun the original FASTA/accession input. A single-sample detector JSON can be re-imported under a descriptive filename; a combined multi-sample JSON does not retain its sample mapping on re-import. Set the filters explicitly and select Run. A form showing default values does not prove those values were used for the retrieved result.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo shows no run log or forgets a new root
docs.text: The saved report omits the run log and input CSV. Check the job status and tree rather than treating a blank log as failure. Rerooting is local to the current page; download the changed Newick. Restoring the job brings back the original tree. Midpoint rooting requires known nonnegative lengths with a positive tree diameter.

docs.title: The array-tree count is smaller than expected
docs.text: Enable Also build array trees before submission. Inspect ZIP index.csv: a single-array group is marked skipped_single_array and has no Newick file. Use (group_id, tree_label) in labels.csv to recover original array identities.

docs.title: ArrayPhyloViz changes disappear or mappings look wrong
docs.text: Use Save changes to create a new private snapshot, or Save project to download editable JSON. Save again after editing merging/order, mapping, styles or layout. An earlier link keeps its earlier state. Assign by leaf uses only the text before the first underscore, so names such as strain_A require another matching rule or manual mapping. Undo an incorrect assignment before continuing.

docs.title: A PDF or example failed to load
docs.text: For ArrayPhyloViz, save the project JSON, reload, restore it and retry PDF; SVG is an alternative. The PDF libraries and CRISPRPrep example files are served with the application. Repeated missing-file errors require an administrator to check deployed static assets. A failed example load does not submit an analysis; select its format again after the assets are available.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: Include the tool name, browser, time of the run, selected settings, exact error message, and the smallest non-sensitive input that reproduces the issue. Do not attach confidential or unpublished sequence data to a public issue.

docs.title: End-to-end workflow
docs.text:
Start at the first step for which you have suitable data. Spacer visualization, tree inference and target searching are separate downstream uses of prepared spacers; target searching is optional and does not need a tree.

View the workflow at full size.

docs.title: 1. Retrieve or collect genome sequences
docs.text:
Use SeqFetcher for nucleotide or GCA_/GCF_ assembly accessions/UIDs, or start with your own genome FASTA. Verify accession, organism and sequence length. Save metadata and maintain a sample list linking each strain to its input records.

Keep contigs from one strain together in a single FASTA file. Separate FASTA files can be submitted together while retaining their sample identities. Protein records are not genome-detection inputs.

docs.title: 2. Detect samples and prepare a combined spacer table
docs.text:
In CRISPRPrep, choose one route:

  • Upload FASTA: up to 100 files / 100 MB, one sample per file. sample_A.fna produces Folder=sample_A.
  • Paste sequence: use >Sample Seq_Name Organism_Name on every record; records sharing Sample belong to the same strain.
  • NCBI accession: up to 100 IDs; retrieved contigs are grouped by the requested accession. Use one assembly accession per strain when available.
  • Import JSON results: one sample per JSON basename. Rename sample_A/result.json to sample_A.json before import if you need Folder=sample_A.

Set evidence/count/direction/N filters and select Run. Review Filtered out arrays and the report, then download Processed CSV, Unprocessed CSV, and the processing report. Save generated CRISPRCasFinder JSON when available and retain your original input separately.

Keep the initial processed CSV from multi-sample detection: re-importing its combined detector JSON treats that file as one sample. To change filters without losing grouping, rerun the original FASTA/accession input or import separate per-sample JSON files. Record processing settings separately; saved reports omit them.

Check these identities in the processed table:

Field Downstream role Folder Strain grouping in CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget. All arrays belonging to one strain should share it. Seq_Name Array identity in SpacerTarget; SpacerMap CSV labels combine Folder_Seq_Name when Folder is present. Check the combined labels for uniqueness. Organism_Name Description-derived organism label and grouping for CRISPRPrep's organism-wide N filter; it is not the strain ID.

docs.title: 3. Infer strain relationships with CRISPRPhylo
docs.text:
Transfer the processed CSV using CRISPRPrep’s CRISPRPhylo link, or paste/upload it to CRISPRPhylo. Confirm at least two usable strain IDs, select GraphMSA or CRISPRFormer and a model profile where applicable, and set Repeat grouping distance (start at 0). Use GraphMSA by default; CRISPRFormer is an option for small datasets, such as 20 strains or fewer. Enable Also build array trees if needed, then select Commit.

Check leaf names and Newick. Download the strain tree, optional array-tree ZIP and result report, and record method/profile and repeat distance. Use midpoint or branch rooting only with a justified interpretation. Download any changed Newick before leaving: the saved job keeps its original root. Tree relationships depend on the retained CRISPR evidence and method; vertical leaf order and completion status are not measures of evolutionary confidence.

docs.title: 4. Compare array structure with SpacerMap
docs.text:
Upload the same processed CSV to SpacerMap, start with Right / No clustering, and select Commit. Review names, order, array-specific triangles and shared IDs. Only interpret leader/trailer ends after confirming orientation from the source data.

Try Shared spacer to inspect groups connected by two or more IDs, or Ancestral spacer to group identical rightmost IDs. Export the array-map SVG to preserve IDs, array membership, order, colors and positions. Download numbered file separately saves a Spacer_ID / Spacer_Sequence mapping, not reusable array rows. Re-numbering a different subset may assign different IDs.

Open Spacer occurrence to inspect the number of arrays containing each spacer ID and, for up to 50 distinct IDs, a bar chart with a presence/absence matrix. Save Download statistics CSV for all IDs, including larger datasets. Count arrays separately from strains when several arrays belong to one strain; repeated copies within one array contribute only once. Keep the original input and identify any subset used for a chart. Use the array-map SVG, rather than the statistics chart, for the integrated figure below.

docs.title: 5. Search candidate targets when relevant
docs.text:
Upload the processed CSV to SpacerTarget, or select the SpacerTarget link below CRISPRPrep’s downloads. Verify that original spacer sequences are 15–100 A/C/G/T bases and that sample IDs are present. Choose the hit limit and select Search.

Save the results link. On completion, inspect Strict matches, open alignments, then compare Exact or Explore if needed. A sequence match does not establish a functional CRISPR target or infection relationship. Download all candidates, the search report and a filtered TSV documenting the evidence used in your study.

Do not substitute SpacerMap numbered TXT: a spacer number has no searchable nucleotide sequence.

docs.title: 6. Compose an integrated figure
docs.text:
Open ArrayPhyloViz, upload Newick and the SpacerMap array-map SVG (or an existing array-per-line TXT), and select Commit.

Match arrays to the original leaf names. SpacerMap CSV labels normally use Folder_Seq_Name, while tree leaves use Folder. Assign by leaf matches the text before the first underscore; use it only when that prefix is the full leaf name. Otherwise use the processed table to assign arrays manually. Review all missing leaves and unassigned arrays. Multiple arrays can belong to one strain.

Adjust label space, row spacing, branch display and annotations. Merge all by leaf can display each leaf's arrays in one row; this preserves every spacer copy and does not infer a biological concatenation. Save project JSON and mapping TSV, then export SVG, PNG or PDF. Use Save changes to preserve the current edited snapshot for recovery through My Jobs. A saved project preserves figure edits; the processed CSV and original JSON preserve their sequence basis.

docs.title: Keep an analysis bundle
docs.text:
Keep sample metadata, original FASTA/JSON, processing report, processed CSV, original numbered arrays if used, spacer ID–sequence mapping, array-map SVG, occurrence statistics CSV/figure when used, Newick, optional target-search report/TSVs, final mapping, editable project and exported figures. Record the analysis date, software version if available, filtering choices, tree method/profile, SpacerMap grouping/alignment/seed and figure edits.

Save private results links as you proceed; My Jobs can restore accepted jobs across devices. Results expire seven days after completion and inputs are deleted at task end, so links do not replace downloaded evidence or a settings record.

See Downloads for a file-by-file guide and Troubleshooting for recovery steps.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
Save the output appropriate to your next step. A private results link restores a job for seven days; it is not a permanent file archive. Tool-specific downloads are available after Open results from My Jobs.

Tool Download Contents and use SeqFetcher FASTA Selected full-length records, deduplicated by returned accession. An assembly contains multiple contigs in one FASTA. SeqFetcher Metadata TSV / ZIP Selected metadata; ZIP adds combined/per-accession FASTA, metadata JSON, run report and failed/pending ID lists. CRISPRPrep CRISPRCasFinder JSON Generated detector output, available for detection jobs. Retains detector annotations. Re-import treats the file as one sample; preserve the initial processed CSV for multi-sample jobs. Uploaded source JSON must be kept separately. CRISPRPrep Unprocessed CSV spacers_unprocessed.csv: spacer rows after evidence/count filtering, before direction/N normalization. CRISPRPrep Processed CSV spacers_processed.csv: filtered/normalized rows and reverse-complement/effective-repeat fields. Use in SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo or SpacerTarget. CRISPRPrep Processing report Counts, warnings, array outcomes and retrieval failures where applicable. Saved processing options are omitted; record them separately. SpacerMap Download numbered file Tab-separated Spacer_ID / Spacer_Sequence lookup in a .txt file. Retains distinct sequence variants per ID, but has no array membership or order. Use the array-map SVG or restored export_text for array reuse. SpacerMap SVG / raster image Array diagram; supported SVG carries editable array metadata. PNG/JPEG/TIFF/WEBP use the chosen DPI. SpacerMap Cluster-network SVG / PNG Network drawing from the cluster preview's own download buttons. SpacerMap Download statistics CSV SpacerMap-occurrence.csv: all IDs and the number of arrays containing each; repeated copies within one array count once. SpacerMap Occurrence SVG / PDF / EPS / PNG / JPG / TIFF / WEBP Complete bar chart and presence/absence matrix for 1–50 distinct IDs. Separate from the array-map SVG; cannot be imported into ArrayPhyloViz as array data. CRISPRPhylo Download .nwk Current displayed tree, including local rerooting. My Jobs' direct tree download retains the original inferred root. CRISPRPhylo Download tree SVG or PNG of the complete current strain tree, independent of zoom/pan. CRISPRPhylo Download array trees (.zip) Optional group Newick files, index.csv, labels.csv and README.txt; enable before running. Not included inside the result JSON. SpacerTarget Export filtered TSV Match rows passing current table filters and node/edge focus, across all table pages. SpacerTarget All candidates TSV All returned alignments without Strict/current table filtering; not an exhaustive database search. SpacerTarget Search report Retained query/occurrence identifiers, match evidence, annotation status and batch history. Terminal reports omit original full sequences, parameters and raw BLAST responses. SpacerTarget PNG / SVG Current association network view. Preserve TSV/report as supporting evidence. ArrayPhyloViz Save project Editable local project JSON with mapping, tree, styles, array merging/order and figure edits. ArrayPhyloViz Save changes A server snapshot of the project with its own ID and expiry; later edits require another save. ArrayPhyloViz Mapping TSV Array-to-leaf assignments, spacer counts and displayed reversals. ArrayPhyloViz SVG / PNG / PDF Complete integrated figure. SVG embeds project data; PDF is downloaded directly and is not a replacement for the editable JSON. ArrayPhyloViz Newick Full tree in edited child order, using original names and branch lengths. Display annotations live in the project. My Jobs Export job links Plain-text links for importing history on another device; no sequence data or figures are included.

docs.title: Does a visible filter affect downloads?
docs.text:
Tool Scope SeqFetcher Selected retrieved rows, including selected rows hidden by search. The header checkbox affects only visible rows. CRISPRPrep All rows produced by the run's processing settings, regardless of preview search/page. SpacerTarget Filtered TSV follows table filters and graph focus; All candidates ignores them. Network type-visibility checkboxes affect the drawing only. SpacerMap Array-map export contains the complete diagram. Statistics CSV includes all IDs, beyond the first 100 table rows; occurrence charts include every ID only when there are 1–50 in total. CRISPRPhylo Complete figure, independent of preview zoom/pan, using the current local root. ArrayPhyloViz Complete figure at selected export resolution; collapsed clades and styles affect the drawing.

SpacerTarget table rows count occurrence–site matches; network edge weights count different supporting query sequences. Those totals need not agree. After input cleanup, the TSV sequence column can be blank while alignment evidence remains; keep original input FASTA/CSV for complete spacer sequences.

SpacerMap occurrence figures use their own format/DPI controls. Raster occurrence exports are capped at 40 million pixels; lower DPI or choose SVG/PDF if necessary. Vector export does not remove the 50-ID chart limit. Archive normalized array text or the array-map SVG with the statistics CSV to preserve array membership and the ID scheme. The separate ID–sequence lookup does not preserve membership.

docs.title: Minimum analysis bundle
docs.text:
Keep original accessions/FASTA/JSON, sample identities, a separate settings record, processing report, processed CSV, normalized array text or array-map SVG, ID–sequence lookup, occurrence CSV/figures when used, original and any rerooted Newick, optional array-tree ZIP, figure mapping/project and final images. For target searches add original spacers, database/hit limit/filter settings, all candidates, filtered TSV and search report.

Record analysis date and software version when available, method/profile, repeat-distance value, processing thresholds, alignment/clustering, color seed and relevant figure edits. Server reports omit some input-related fields by design; do not rely on a result link alone to reproduce an analysis.

docs.title: Input formats
docs.text: Use this page to choose the correct input and preserve sample identities. Save text files as UTF-8. Examples are illustrative, not biological validation datasets.

docs.title: Which file goes where?
docs.text: File/data Tool NCBI sequence accessions or UIDs SeqFetcher; nucleotide IDs also work in CRISPRPrep’s NCBI accession mode GCA_/GCF_ assembly accession SeqFetcher in Nucleotide mode, or CRISPRPrep’s NCBI accession mode Genome/contig FASTA CRISPRPrep detection: one sample per uploaded file, or explicit sample fields in pasted headers CRISPRCasFinder JSON CRISPRPrep; SpacerMap and SpacerTarget accept it with different filtering rules Processed spacer CSV SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo, SpacerTarget Spacer FASTA SpacerMap or SpacerTarget, with different grouping conventions below Numbered arrays (one array per line) SpacerMap and ArrayPhyloViz; not SpacerTarget or CRISPRPhylo SpacerMap Spacer_ID / Spacer_Sequence mapping Output lookup table; does not contain array membership and is not array input Newick tree plus arrays ArrayPhyloViz Saved ArrayPhyloViz project JSON ArrayPhyloViz Open saved project

docs.title: Genome FASTA
docs.text:
CRISPRPrep accepts up to 100 uploaded .fa, .fasta or .fna files, 100 MB combined. Each file is one sample; its basename without the extension becomes Folder. Multiple contigs in that file share the sample. Uploaded FASTA uses ordinary headers:

>contig_1 Example organism strain A
ATGCGTACGTTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGC
>contig_2 Example organism strain A
GGCATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGTTA

Each file needs unique, nonempty sequence IDs. IDs may contain letters, digits, underscores, dots, colons, pipes, + and -. Sequences must use IUPAC DNA letters.

Pasted FASTA has a different header contract: >Sample Seq_Name Organism_Name. The first two fields cannot contain spaces; all remaining header text is the organism description. Repeat Sample for contigs belonging to one strain and keep Seq_Name unique within that sample:

>sample_A contig_1 Example organism strain A
ATGCGTACGTTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGC
>sample_B contig_1 Example organism strain B
GGCATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGTTA

These short sequences demonstrate syntax only. Pasted input is limited to 100 MB. FASTA sequence IDs are restored after any detector-only renaming; CSV Seq_Name instead follows the detector's CRISPR array Name. Duplicate sample/array names receive suffixes.

docs.title: NCBI ID list
docs.text: Use one or more nucleotide IDs such as NC_012920.1 or NM_000546.6, or protein IDs such as NP_000537.3 in a separate Protein run. Newlines, commas, spaces and semicolons separate IDs. Uploaded TXT/CSV/TSV must contain IDs only, with no column header. Sequence UIDs are accepted. GCA_/GCF_ assembly accessions are accepted in Nucleotide mode, for example GCF_000339015.1. They identify an assembly whose downloaded FASTA preserves separate chromosome/contig records. Gene, Taxonomy, BioProject and SRA IDs are not supported. CRISPRPrep accepts up to 100 nucleotide/assembly IDs and combines successful records into one detection input while preserving the requested ID as Sample / Folder; assembly contigs share that ID and aliases use the first successfully retrieved ID; SeqFetcher accepts up to 500 IDs. Both submitted ID lists are limited to 16,000 characters.

docs.title: CRISPRCasFinder JSON
docs.text:
Provide the detector's result object containing Sequences, each sequence's Crisprs, and each array's Regions. Keep the original JSON for reprocessing. In CRISPRPrep, sample names come from JSON basenames without .json, not parent directories: sample_A/result.json becomes result. Rename it to sample_A.json to preserve that sample name. A combined multi-sample detector JSON is treated as one sample on re-import; retain the original processed CSV and input sample manifest.

Import destination What happens CRISPRPrep Adjustable evidence/count filters plus optional unknown-direction and organism-wide N exclusion. Default minimum evidence is 1 and minimum spacer count is 2. SpacerMap Fixed evidence 3–4 filtering, unresolved ND removal and organism-wide N exclusion. SpacerTarget Retains all spacer regions regardless of evidence/direction; each JSON file is one sample. Every sequence must still pass its 15–100 A/C/G/T validation.

Use CRISPRPrep if filtering needs to be explicit and documented. A processing report, target-search report or figure-project JSON is not interchangeable with detector JSON. CRISPRPrep’s CRISPRCasFinder JSON download supplies generated detector output; keep any JSON you upload separately, because saved jobs do not retain those uploads.

docs.title: Processed spacer CSV
docs.text:
Each row is one spacer occurrence. CRISPRPhylo requires this complete header; CRISPRPrep output includes additional useful columns:

Folder,Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence,DR_Consensus,Reverse_Complement_Sequence,Reverse_Complement_DR
strain_A,strain_A_CRISPR1,+,ACGTACGT,TGCA,,
strain_A,strain_A_CRISPR1,+,GATTACAA,TGCA,,
strain_B,strain_B_CRISPR1,-,ACTTAGCA,GCAT,TGCTAAGT,ATGC
strain_B,strain_B_CRISPR1,-,GCCATGGA,GCAT,TCCATGGC,ATGC

This is a format illustration; its short spacers are not suitable SpacerTarget input. Use actual processed data for analysis. Keep rows from each array in their intended order, and retain reverse-complement columns supplied by CRISPRPrep.

Field Identity rule Folder Strain ID for CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget. Do not merge different strains under the same value. Seq_Name Array ID. For CSV, SpacerMap combines nonempty Folder and Seq_Name as Folder_Seq_Name; without Folder it uses Seq_Name alone. Keep the resulting labels unique. Organism_Name Description-derived label, used by CRISPRPrep's organism-wide N filter; not a substitute for strain ID.

SpacerMap accepts pasted CSV as well as uploaded CSV when its header includes Spacer_Sequence. Its minimum custom CSV header is Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence. It skips Orientation=ND, rejects conflicting orientations within one combined array label, and can compute a missing negative-strand reverse complement. It preserves CSV row order for both strands, so supply the already normalized CRISPRPrep Processed CSV rather than reversing negative arrays again. CRISPRPhylo requires all seven columns and a usable reverse-complement spacer value for reverse rows. Effective_DR in CRISPRPrep output is the orientation-appropriate repeat.

docs.title: Numbered arrays
docs.text:
Use one array per line. A tab separates the unique name from its spacer IDs; commas, spaces or semicolons separate IDs.

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8

Download this example. IDs identify types within the dataset, not globally across runs. Generate IDs for all arrays together in SpacerMap and preserve the array-map SVG or normalized array text. Its Download numbered file output is the sequence lookup below, not array-per-line TXT. DNA arrays in uploaded TXT/TSV can be converted automatically by SpacerMap; pasted array-format text treats tokens as labels; a recognized spacer CSV is converted through the CSV route.

docs.title: Spacer ID–sequence mapping
docs.text:
SpacerMap's Download numbered file writes a tab-separated .txt with this header:

Spacer_ID   Spacer_Sequence
1   ACGTACGT

The header is literal and case-sensitive. Each distinct (ID, sequence) pair is retained; similarity-grouped variants can share an ID and occupy separate rows. Negative-strand CSV spacers use the reverse-complement sequence used for numbering. This table has no array names, memberships or order. Do not upload it as numbered-array input to SpacerMap or ArrayPhyloViz; use the array-map SVG for the latter, or preserve the original array-per-line text. Number-only input has no sequence mapping. Rerun older saved results from original sequence input if the mapping is needed.

docs.title: Spacer occurrence outputs
docs.text:
Download statistics CSV in SpacerMap produces a result table with this header:

Spacer ID,Number of arrays
"2",3
"6",3

Each row counts the arrays containing one ID, counting repeated copies within an array once. This is an output summary, not a numbered-array input or a sequence table for any downstream tool. Use the complete example CSV to inspect the format. Preserve the numbered arrays to retain array membership and order.

The occurrence SVG contains a bar chart and presence/absence matrix. It does not contain editable array-map metadata. For ArrayPhyloViz, use the array-map SVG or numbered arrays instead of occurrence or cluster-network figures.

docs.title: Spacer FASTA and direction folders
docs.text:
For SpacerMap, one uploaded FASTA represents one array, each record one spacer. Numeric record headers are used directly as IDs; other headers trigger sequence-based numbering. For multiple arrays, choose a folder such as:

dataset/
  pos/
    strain_A.fasta
    strain_B.fasta
  neg/
    strain_C.fasta

Folder names containing pos/forward or neg/reverse identify direction. Either side can be absent. Relative paths contribute to array names, so you may need manual matching to tree leaves later. Supply spacer records, not whole contigs.

For SpacerTarget, use >strain|array|spacer to encode sample identity:

>strain_A|CRISPR1|spacer_1
CGCCAGGGTTTTCCCAGTCACGACGTTGTAAA

Each sequence must be 15–100 A/C/G/T bases. Download an example. Alternatively use a header such as >spacer_1 strain=strain_A array=CRISPR1 source=NC_000000.1, replacing the placeholder source accession. Without strain metadata, matches appear in the table but not the strain network.

SpacerTarget CSV/TSV requires sequence or Spacer_Sequence. Supported metadata includes strain_id (aliases strain, Folder), strain_name, array_id (alias Seq_Name), spacer_id, orientation (alias Orientation) and source_accession. Sequence-only tables are searchable but lack strain mapping.

docs.title: Newick
docs.text:
ArrayPhyloViz accepts one Newick tree with unique leaf names and a final semicolon:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);

Download this illustrative tree. Colon values are branch lengths; 95 is an internal label supplied by the input. Quoted labels are accepted. Bracket comments are ignored. Matching uses original leaf names, not edited display labels.

docs.title: Array-tree ZIP
docs.text: Enable Also build array trees in CRISPRPhylo before running. Each group_*.nwk contains arrays from one repeat group. index.csv lists built and skipped groups; labels.csv maps each (group_id, tree_label) to an original array UID. Use both columns to recover labels correctly. This ZIP is an output bundle, not an input accepted directly by the tree builder or ArrayPhyloViz. Extract the intended Newick and prepare array names/mapping for that specific tree.

docs.title: Editable figure data
docs.text: Use Save project in ArrayPhyloViz to produce crisprevo-composer version 1 JSON, then Open saved project to restore it. Do not manually change node IDs; annotations depend on them. The array-upload control also accepts supported crisprevo-spacermap version 1 metadata JSON and SVG files carrying supported SpacerMap/ArrayPhyloViz metadata. Arbitrary JSON and image screenshots are not substitutes. Save changes stores an ArrayPhyloViz snapshot for seven-day recovery; Save project downloads the local reusable file.

docs.title: Limits and retention
docs.text:
These limits reflect the current code. MB-labelled CRISPRPrep and SpacerTarget input limits use 1,048,576 bytes per MB. A hosting proxy can impose stricter upload limits. An accepted job can wait in a queue before its analysis begins; a busy response without a Job ID requires a later resubmission.

Tool / area Limit SeqFetcher 500 unique IDs; 16,000 submitted ID-text characters; ID-list file up to 1 MB SeqFetcher requests At most 5 IDs per request; assembly-containing lists automatically use 1 SeqFetcher response 8 million residues per batch, including all contigs of an assembly SeqFetcher saved FASTA 25 million characters per job, including headers/newlines NCBI assembly package 64 MiB downloaded or expanded package size CRISPRPrep input 100 MB combined; up to 100 uploaded FASTA or imported JSON files; pasted FASTA up to 100 MB CRISPRPrep NCBI accession input 100 unique nucleotide/assembly IDs and 16,000 text characters; combined retrieved FASTA up to 100 MB CRISPRPrep extraction 100,000 arrays or extracted spacer rows CRISPRPrep minimum-spacer option Integer 1–10,000; default 2 CRISPR detection runtime Up to 2 hours for detection; queue waiting can add elapsed time. The service may stop a run earlier CRISPRPhylo runtime 15 minutes for inference; queue waiting is separate CRISPRPhylo repeat-distance option Nonnegative integer; default 0 SpacerTarget uploaded input 100 MB combined, up to 100 files SpacerTarget pasted input 2 MB SpacerTarget sequence format Each spacer 15–100 A/C/G/T bases SpacerTarget queries / occurrences 100 distinct sequences / 10,000 occurrences SpacerTarget search batches At most 10 distinct sequences and 1,000 bases per batch SpacerTarget target limit 20, 50 (default), or 100 targets per spacer SpacerTarget network Up to 200 displayed nodes; tables/exports retain all filtered rows SpacerTarget submitted search A batch exceeding 24 hours is marked failed ArrayPhyloViz Newick One tree, up to 1 MB ArrayPhyloViz tree 1,000 leaves, 4,000 nodes, depth 250 ArrayPhyloViz array text 4 MB ArrayPhyloViz arrays 1,500 arrays; 2,000 spacers per array; 20,000 total instances ArrayPhyloViz / CRISPRPhylo PNG 32 million pixels and at most 16,000 pixels per side SpacerMap raster DPI 36–2,400; default 300 SpacerMap occurrence chart 1–50 distinct IDs; above 50, chart preview and chart export are disabled, without truncation SpacerMap occurrence table / CSV First 100 IDs on page; all IDs in statistics CSV SpacerMap occurrence raster export 40 million pixels; lower DPI or choose SVG/PDF My Jobs bulk link import 100 links/IDs per import Saved results and task records Seven days after the task ends

docs.title: Queue capacity
docs.text:
Jobs may wait when the service is busy. If a Job ID has been issued, keep the results link and wait for the existing job. If submission is rejected before a Job ID appears, retry after the interval shown on screen. Queue time depends on workload and dataset size.

An accepted Waiting for resources job keeps its input while queued and has no result-expiry timestamp until it ends. Keep its ID instead of repeatedly resubmitting. A 503 busy response before an ID is issued means the submission was rejected; retry after the displayed interval . See My Jobs.

docs.title: What survives closing the page?
docs.text:
Once a Job ID appears, the accepted analysis continues on the server. Save its private link and retrieve it through My Jobs. The default browser history lasts only for the tab; Remember job history on this device preserves references locally but does not extend server retention.

Original input workspaces are deleted when a task ends. Saved outputs are not a complete archive of uploads, settings or logs. Keep those separately. Further ArrayPhyloViz edits need Save changes or a downloaded project; CRISPRPhylo rerooting changes only the current view/download, not the saved original tree.

For larger data, split analyses into biologically meaningful groups and use SVG for large figures. Download important results before expiry; opening a result link does not reset its expiry time.

docs.title: CRISPRPrep
docs.text: Use CRISPRPrep (/crispr-processing) to detect CRISPR arrays in genome sequences or prepare existing CRISPRCasFinder results. It produces a filtered spacer CSV for SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget, plus a report explaining what was retained or excluded.

docs.title: Upload genome FASTA
docs.text:
1. Select Detect from sequence → Upload FASTA.
  2. Add .fa, .fasta or .fna files: up to 100 files and 100 MB combined. Each file represents one sample and may contain multiple contigs.
  3. Use ordinary FASTA headers such as >contig_1 organism description, with unique sequence IDs within each file and IUPAC DNA sequence on following lines.
  4. Use Add files or drag more files into the upload area to append files from other folders. Check the accumulated list; an invalid addition leaves the previous selection intact. Reset clears it.
  5. Check detector availability with Refresh status, configure processing, then select Run.

The sample and CSV Folder are the basename without the final .fa, .fasta or .fna extension: sample_A.fna becomes sample_A. All contigs in that file share the sample. Duplicate sample names receive numeric suffixes. Give different strains different filenames; several files can be detected in one run. Current upload help text may still say that the extension is included; the parser removes it.

Sequence IDs that collide across samples are temporarily distinguished for detection and restored in the downloadable detector JSON. CSV Seq_Name comes from the detected CRISPR array Name, with suffixes added to distinguish duplicate array names; it is not the FASTA record ID alone.

Detection requires a configured Linux detector. If it is unavailable, import existing CRISPRCasFinder JSON. Detection can run for up to two hours, separate from queue waiting; the service may stop a run earlier. Once a Job ID appears, detection and processing continue after closing the page. Save Copy results link and return through My Jobs. Results expire seven days after the task ends.

The bundled detector enables Cas-gene analysis by default when configured with CCF_ENABLE_CAS=1. Available Cas annotations remain in CRISPRCasFinder JSON; the spacer CSV and array table are not Cas-system reports. Administrators can disable Cas analysis. Intermediate Cas files and run logs are not user downloads.

docs.title: Paste sequence with explicit sample names
docs.text:
Select Detect from sequence → Paste sequence. Every header must have three fields:

>Sample Seq_Name Organism_Name

The first field supplies Sample / Folder, the second is the original sequence ID, and the remaining text is the organism description, which can contain spaces. Repeat the same Sample for contigs belonging to one strain; the (Sample, Seq_Name) pair must be unique. Sample and sequence ID cannot contain spaces. For example:

>sample_A contig_1 Example organism strain A
ATGCGTACGTTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGC
>sample_A contig_2 Example organism strain A
GGCATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGTTA
>sample_B contig_1 Example organism strain B
ATGCGTACGTTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGC

These short records demonstrate syntax only. Pasted FASTA is limited to 100 MB. Ordinary uploaded-file headers do not automatically satisfy the paste contract; add the explicit Sample field before pasting. Both modes preserve sample identity through CSV processing.

docs.title: Fetch from NCBI and detect automatically
docs.text:
1. Select Detect from sequence → NCBI accession.
  2. Paste up to 100 unique nucleotide accessions, nucleotide sequence UIDs, or assembly accessions (GCA_/GCF_). Separate IDs with newlines, spaces, commas or semicolons; the text limit is 16,000 characters.
  3. Set processing filters, select Run, and save the private results link.
  4. Follow retrieval, detection and processing progress. Successful records proceed even when some IDs fail.
  5. Review Accession IDs needing attention and the retrieval summary before interpreting the arrays.

For example, GCF_000339015.1 retrieves an assembly with its component contigs, whereas NC_000913.3 requests one nucleotide record. Each retrieved sequence is assigned to the requested accession ID in Sample / Folder; all contigs of an assembly share that requested ID. Aliases resolving to a previously retrieved accession use the first successful input ID and do not create another copy. This is accession deduplication, not sequence-similarity clustering.

Successful sequences are combined into one detector FASTA, within a 100 MB total limit, while retaining their sample mapping for the processed CSV. Several requested contig IDs from the same biological strain still become separate sample IDs: use a single assembly accession or one uploaded FASTA per strain when that grouping is required. If the task is partial, inspect failures and retry needed IDs in a new submission.

docs.title: Import JSON results
docs.text:
1. Select Import JSON results.
  2. Upload up to 100 CRISPRCasFinder JSON files, within 100 MB combined, or use Choose a results folder to select JSON files recursively.
  3. Add further files through Add files or drag-and-drop if needed.
  4. Configure filters and select Run.

The sample is the JSON basename without .json, even for a folder upload. sample_A/result.json becomes result, not sample_A; repeated basenames become result_2, result_3, and so on. Rename files to descriptive sample names such as sample_A.json before import. The currently displayed hint about keeping the extension is outdated.

While source JSON is loaded locally, Original JSON → Download JSON downloads the selected file before processing. Uploaded source JSON is not retained in saved results.

A generated multi-sample detection JSON does not embed the separate sample mapping used for that job's CSV processing. Re-importing it treats the whole file as one sample. Keep the initial processed CSV and sample manifest; to re-filter a multi-sample detection, rerun the original FASTA/accession input with the new settings, or prepare separate correctly named JSON files per sample.

docs.title: Try the supplied examples
docs.text:
Select Load example, then choose a format. Loading fills the corresponding input and resets processing options to their defaults; select Run to submit.

Example option Loaded data Requires detection? Upload FASTA Five genome files: 702, CFSAN134858, CFSAN134971, CS-54 and ES191; about 23 MB in total. Yes Paste sequence The same genomes combined into 416 records with explicit Sample / sequence / organism headers. Yes NCBI accession Five assembly IDs. Yes, plus NCBI retrieval Import JSON results Five precomputed CRISPRCasFinder JSON files. No

With the bundled JSON examples and default filters, expect 95 inspected arrays, 10 retained arrays and 119 processed spacer rows. These are precomputed-example counts, not guaranteed counts from a new detection run.

The example replaces the current selection only after loading successfully. If a download fails, retry the desired format; the previous input remains available.

docs.title: Set processing options
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect and when to change it Minimum evidence level All evidence levels (1) Inclusive threshold: 3 keeps levels 3 and 4. Use a higher threshold to restrict the result to higher-evidence detector calls. At level 1, missing evidence values are also retained; thresholds 2–4 exclude them. Minimum spacers per array 2 Keeps arrays with at least this many Spacer regions. Increase to exclude shorter arrays; decrease to 1 if single-spacer arrays are relevant. Remove unknown orientation (ND) Checked Excludes unresolved direction after trying CRISPRDirection as a fallback. Unchecking retains unknown-direction arrays without inferring an orientation. Exclude organisms with N-containing spacers Checked Removes all extracted rows with the same organism name if any extracted spacer in that group contains N. It can affect multiple files in the batch.

Evidence levels are detector categories, not probabilities or a percentage confidence. These options filter detector results; they do not change the detector's search parameters.

The N filter is organism-wide, not limited to the single spacer, array or sample. Identical organism descriptions across files are grouped together; empty descriptions are also grouped together. If many otherwise usable arrays disappear, examine this filter and the report before concluding that those samples lack arrays. Other ambiguous DNA letters can still remain; SpacerTarget requires A/C/G/T only.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
Start with the summary: input files and detected arrays describe what was inspected; retained arrays and processed spacer rows describe what remains after filtering. Extracted spacer rows have passed evidence and minimum-count filters; processed rows have additionally passed the chosen direction/N rules.

The array table has one row per detected array:

Column How to read it Sample / array Sample grouping and array name; use these to trace the record to your input. Duplicate array names are made unique across the batch. Organism Name taken from the sequence description, not a new taxonomic identification. Evidence CRISPRCasFinder evidence category, or missing if not provided. Direction Resolved +/-, or unresolved ND. Spacers Number of spacer regions reported for that array before final filtering. Processing result Retained or the applicable reason for exclusion.

Select Filtered out to investigate missing arrays. Typical reasons are Below evidence threshold, Unknown evidence, Too few spacers, Unknown orientation, and Organism contains N. An array may violate several rules; the displayed reason is not necessarily every possible reason. Zero retained arrays can be a valid filtering outcome, not a failed run.

Expand Preview processed spacer rows to inspect the first 200 rows. Original sequence and reverse complement are separate fields; blank reverse-complement cells for positive arrays are expected. Effective repeat is the orientation-appropriate repeat for that row. For negative arrays, processing reverses spacer row order within the array and adds reverse-complement sequence/repeat fields. It does not overwrite the original spacer sequence.

Search, status filters and pagination affect the preview only. Downloads include all rows from the applied settings. To change filtering, reselect your original JSON files or rerun the original detection input with new options and select Run. A single-sample detector JSON can also be re-imported under a descriptive filename. Re-importing a combined multi-sample JSON loses its original sample grouping. Saved results omit the original uploaded files and processing options. The current form values must not be assumed to describe a restored result; record your chosen settings separately.

docs.title: Choose downloads and next steps
docs.text:
Download Contents Next use CRISPRCasFinder JSON Generated result.json, available for detection jobs including accession-based detection. Preserves detector annotations and restored sequence names. Re-import only with the sample-grouping caveat above. Keep uploaded JSON separately; it is not retained as a saved job output. Unprocessed CSV Folder, Organism_Name, Seq_Name, Orientation, Spacer_Sequence, DR_Consensus. Inspect rows after evidence/count filtering. Processed CSV Extracted fields plus Reverse_Complement_Sequence, Reverse_Complement_DR, Effective_DR; applies direction/N rules. Input for SpacerMap and CRISPRPhylo; original spacer sequences also support SpacerTarget. Download processing report Counts, warnings, array outcomes and retrieval summary where applicable. Saved reports omit processing options. Explain exclusions; retain a separate settings record for reproducibility.

Select the CRISPRPhylo, SpacerMap or SpacerTarget link below the downloads to transfer the processed CSV into that tool in the same tab. Review the imported input, then submit it there; transfer does not start another analysis. If browser storage prevents transfer, download Processed CSV and upload it manually.

For tree building, confirm that Folder represents the intended strains. For array plotting, preserve unique Seq_Name values. See Input formats for their different roles.

docs.title: Limits and common problems
docs.text:
Up to 100 MB total input, 100 uploaded FASTA or imported JSON files, and 100,000 parsed arrays or extracted spacer rows are accepted. Empty results still download as CSV with headers.

Symptom Action JSON rejected Supply a CRISPRCasFinder result containing Sequences, Crisprs and Regions, not a saved figure project or processing report. Many arrays unexpectedly excluded Review evidence, direction, count and organism-wide N filtering. Only one strain appears downstream Check input grouping: one sample per uploaded FASTA, explicit Sample fields for pasted FASTA, requested IDs for NCBI, or basenames for JSON. Re-imported combined JSON becomes one sample. Refreshed job cannot be recovered Retrieve the full ID/private link in My Jobs. After seven-day expiry, rerun with your saved input.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo
docs.text: Use CRISPRPhylo (/tree-builder) to infer strain relationships from CRISPR spacer data. You can also request separate array trees within repeat groups. The page displays the strain tree, supports interactive rooting, and exports Newick and tree images. Use ArrayPhyloViz to combine a chosen tree with arrays.

docs.title: Prepare a processed spacer CSV
docs.text:
Use Processed CSV from CRISPRPrep, either transferred through its CRISPRPhylo link or uploaded manually. Each row is one spacer; keep the order within each array. All seven columns must be present, even when some cells are empty:

Folder,Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence,DR_Consensus,Reverse_Complement_Sequence,Reverse_Complement_DR
Field Meaning / check Folder Strain ID. Use the same ID for all arrays from one strain and distinct IDs for different strains. Seq_Name Array ID, consistent across spacer rows from that array. Orientation For -, reverse or reversed, the input validation uses the reverse-complement spacer column. Spacer_Sequence Original spacer sequence; used for other orientations. DR_Consensus Array repeat sequence; preserve the detector-derived value. Reverse_Complement_Sequence Required usable spacer sequence for reverse rows. Blank values can make those rows unusable. Reverse_Complement_DR Reverse-complement repeat; CRISPRPrep supplies it for negative arrays.

At least two distinct nonempty strain IDs and two usable spacer rows are required. This minimum does not guarantee informative cross-strain evidence. In particular, CRISPRFormer cannot infer a strain tree if no repeat group contains arrays from two different strains. Numbered TXT, genome FASTA and an unprocessed CSV lacking required columns are not valid substitutes.

docs.title: Select the method and settings
docs.text:
Use GraphMSA by default. For a small dataset, such as 20 strains or fewer, you can choose CRISPRFormer. For larger datasets, use GraphMSA. The 20-strain guideline is a practical recommendation, not an input limit.

Setting Default Recommendation Tree Inference method GraphMSA Keep GraphMSA for routine analyses and larger datasets. Choose CRISPRFormer for small datasets, for example 20 strains or fewer. Model profile (CRISPRFormer) High-variation data Start with the default. Select Conservative data or Mixed data when that profile better matches your dataset. Repeat grouping distance 0 Nonnegative edit-distance tolerance; keep 0 initially. Its meaning differs by method, as explained below. Also build array trees Unchecked Enable before submission if you also need separate array trees, downloaded together as a ZIP.

The Repeat grouping distance label is broader than its current implementation. For CRISPRFormer, it sets the Levenshtein edit-distance threshold for repeat grouping (substitutions, insertions and deletions). For GraphMSA, the web adapter passes it as the spacer Levenshtein-distance tolerance within exact repeat families; increasing it does not merge different repeat families. Record both the method and value, and do not interpret an identical nonzero value as an equivalent setting across methods.

docs.title: Submit and recover a run
docs.text:
1. Select the method, repeat-distance value and optional model profile.
  2. Check Also build array trees if needed. It cannot be added to a completed result without a new run.
  3. Paste CSV or upload one file; use only one input method. Load example supplies trial data.
  4. Select Commit. After a run the same submit control may read Build tree.
  5. Wait for the Job ID, then save Copy results link. Processing continues after the tab closes.
  6. Return through My Jobs or Retrieve previous results to inspect and download the result.

The inference process has a 15-minute limit; queue waiting is separate. Results expire seven days after the task ends. Keep the original CSV and a settings record for reruns. The saved result report retains method/profile, repeat distance and counts, but not the submitted CSV or full run log. A blank Run log in a restored result does not by itself indicate failure.

docs.title: Read the strain tree
docs.text:
Leaves are strains. Check that leaf names correspond to the intended Folder values. The saved report's strain count and usable spacer-row count describe the validated input, not statistical support; spacer rows are occurrences rather than distinct spacer types. Check the actual leaves too, since the inference depends on available repeat-group evidence.

Branching shows inferred grouping. Vertical order is a drawing arrangement, so adjacent labels are not necessarily the closest pair. A CRISPR-based grouping alone does not establish transmission or a whole-genome relationship.

Lengths and rooting need separate interpretation. Numbers after colons in View Newick source are branch lengths. Positive supplied lengths guide horizontal distances in the drawing; otherwise the viewer uses topology spacing. Do not interpret the tree as elapsed time without independent calibration. The web workflow does not add a separate bootstrap-confidence assessment.

For example, ((strain_A:0.1,strain_B:0.1):0.2,strain_C:0.3); groups A and B together in that rooted representation. The numeric branch lengths are not support percentages.

Drag inside the viewer to pan and use Ctrl + scroll (Command + scroll on Mac) to zoom. Scrolling without a modifier scrolls the page. With the viewer focused, use + / - to zoom and Home to fit the complete tree. The initial tree is fitted automatically.

docs.title: Choose a root
docs.text:
Control Effect Midpoint root Places the root halfway along the longest leaf-to-leaf path. Requires known nonnegative lengths on every edge and at least one positive length. Root on branch Enters branch-selection mode. Click a branch at the desired position to place a root there. Keyboard activation of a focused branch selects its midpoint. Restore original root Returns to the original inferred tree supplied by the saved result.

Press Escape to leave branch-selection mode. Midpoint rooting can be unavailable for trees with missing, negative or all-zero branch lengths. Use branch rooting only when you have a justified interpretation, such as an appropriate outgroup; a chosen display root is not new evidence for ancestry.

Root changes update the displayed tree, Newick source and downloads in the current page. The saved job retains its original tree. Download the changed Newick before leaving if you need to preserve that root, and use that downloaded tree in ArrayPhyloViz. Downloading directly from My Jobs retrieves the original saved tree.

docs.title: Read optional array trees
docs.text:
When requested, Array trees reports the generated count and offers Download array trees (.zip). There are no individual array-tree previews on this page; the main preview remains the strain tree.

ZIP member How to use it group_*.nwk A tree of arrays within one repeat family/group. These leaves represent arrays, not one leaf per strain. index.csv Group identifier, array count, tree filename and status. skipped_single_array means the group contained only one array and has no tree. labels.csv Use both group_id and tree_label to recover the original array_uid and identify strain/array membership. Labels are unique within a group, not necessarily across all groups. README.txt Description of the archive and its label mapping.

Array trees reuse the distances from the same analysis. Different files are separate within-group comparisons, not branches of one combined array tree. A count of zero can mean no group had enough arrays; inspect index.csv before treating it as an export failure. The ZIP is a separate download and is not embedded in the JSON report. It remains available from restored results until job expiry.

docs.title: Export and continue
docs.text:
Select Download .nwk for the currently displayed root. Choose SVG or PNG, then Download tree, for an image of the complete current tree independent of pan/zoom. PNG uses 2× rendering and is limited to 32 million pixels and 16,000 pixels per side; use SVG for larger trees.

Keep the input CSV, settings, original Newick, any rerooted Newick, and optional array-tree ZIP. Open ArrayPhyloViz, add the chosen Newick and corresponding SpacerMap array-map SVG or existing array-per-line TXT, and review mapping: tree leaves use strain Folder, whereas SpacerMap CSV array names use Folder_Seq_Name when Folder is present. Assign by leaf handles prefixes without underscores; otherwise review mapping manually. SpacerMap's ID–sequence mapping download is not array-per-line TXT. Multiple arrays may belong to one strain.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Action Missing columns or too few valid rows Use CRISPRPrep Processed CSV; check strain IDs and orientation-specific sequence fields. No cross-strain repeat group Check repeat sequences and sample grouping. For CRISPRFormer, reconsider repeat tolerance only if biologically justified. Missing code/model or no output tree Save the Job ID/error and contact the site administrator. Midpoint root disabled Inspect Newick lengths; missing, negative or all-zero lengths do not meet the requirements. A root change disappeared on reopening Expected: the job stores the original tree. Use the rerooted Newick you downloaded. Array-tree ZIP missing Confirm the option was enabled before submission; reopen interactive results rather than the generic report download.

docs.title: ArrayPhyloViz
docs.text: Use ArrayPhyloViz (/figure-composer) to align CRISPR arrays beside an existing tree, annotate the figure and export an editable project. It does not infer a new tree, reroot the tree or change branch lengths. Supply a tree from CRISPRPhylo or another analysis and arrays from SpacerMap.

docs.title: Load a tree and arrays
docs.text:
1. Under Phylogenetic tree, paste one Newick tree or upload .nwk, .newick, .tree or .txt.
  2. Under CRISPR arrays, paste numbered arrays or upload TXT/TSV, supported array JSON, or a newly exported SpacerMap SVG.
  3. Choose the name-matching rule, then select Commit. The tool composes the figure and attempts to save an initial private-link snapshot.
  4. Open Review and edit mapping before interpreting the figure.

For a first trial, select Load example, then Commit: the built-in dataset has eight leaves (C01–C08) and nine arrays and selects suffix matching. Alternatively, paste the following three-leaf walkthrough data with Exact names:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8

Newick requires unique leaf names and a final semicolon. Quoted labels are supported. Plain internal labels and branch lengths are retained; bracket comments are ignored. In this illustrative tree, 95 is an input internal label: ArrayPhyloViz displays it but does not calculate or validate its statistical meaning.

Use the array-map SVG from SpacerMap to preserve colors and source alignment positions. Occurrence charts and cluster-network SVGs do not carry the editable array-map data and cannot be used instead. Use one-array-per-line numbered TXT when only names, IDs and order are needed.
